cases.title: `^build` builds every dependency before the project that needs it
Running one project's task runs what it depends on, and nothing else
A bare name in dependsOn waits on the same project’s task
`lib#build` in dependsOn runs that task first, with no package dependency
A dependency two projects share builds once per run
`^build` reaches a dependency’s dependency when the middle project has no build
cases.why: app reads lib’s output through mid; skipping lib leaves app reading nothing.

cases.title: Running a library’s task does not run the projects that depend on it
A task only some projects declare runs in exactly those
A project whose directory holds spaces builds, caches and restores
A task named `test:unit` runs as its own task
A second run over an unchanged tree replays instead of running
Editing an input runs the task again
A same-size edit right after a commit runs the task again
A new file under an input glob runs the task again
Deleting an input runs the task again
Renaming an input runs the task again
An edit deep in a nested input directory runs the task again
An edit to an input named with spaces, `$` and quotes runs the task again
An edit to an input with a non-ASCII name runs the task again
Undoing an edit replays the first run’s outputs, not the edited ones
A file outside the task’s inputs changes nothing
A file a `!` input pattern takes back changes nothing
A gitignored file under an input glob changes nothing
cases.why: Ignored files are local state (logs, caches); keying on them makes every machine miss.

cases.title: A new file git does not track yet is an input
Making an input executable runs the task again
cases.why: The mode is part of what the task reads: a build that copies a script ships it runnable or not.

cases.title: Editing a dependency rebuilds the projects that read its output
Editing one project does not rerun a project that does not depend on it
An edit to a file outside a dependency’s build inputs does not rebuild its dependents

cases.title: Pointing an input symlink at another file runs the task again
A task that lists no inputs never replays a stale result when a file it reads changes
cases.why: A default guesses what the task reads; a file outside the guess changes and the cache replays the old bytes.

cases.title: A task that lists no inputs never replays a stale result when a variable it reads changes
cases.why: A cache keyed on files alone replays the output of a value the command no longer sees.

cases.title: A task that lists no inputs runs again when its project’s sources change
Deleted outputs come back from the cache with the same bytes
Deleted outputs are restored, not rebuilt
An output edited by hand is put back on the next run
cases.why: The run’s result is the tree the inputs produce; a hand edit left in place ships bytes no build made.

cases.title: A rebuild leaves no output the new inputs no longer produce
cases.why: A file a renamed source used to produce would otherwise ship from dist forever.

cases.title: Restoring an older entry leaves no file a later build added
cases.why: The restored tree must be the one that entry’s inputs produce.

cases.title: A stray file dropped in an output directory is gone after a restore
cases.why: Outputs are what the task wrote; a leftover file in dist ships in the package.

cases.title: Only declared outputs are restored
A `!` output pattern keeps that file out of the cache
An executable output comes back executable
A symlink output comes back as the same link
Nested output directories and binary bytes restore intact
A dependency’s deleted outputs are back before a rebuilding dependent reads them
Two projects with the same command and the same sources keep their own outputs
cases.why: The command runs in each project’s own directory; one project’s bytes restored into the other is a wrong tree.

cases.title: A replayed task that lists no outputs leaves a file it wrote, and the user then edited, alone
cases.why: A default guesses what the task writes; restoring a file nobody declared overwrites the user’s bytes with an old copy.

nx.detail: a#build replayed and left packages/a/dist/report.txt "report\n", expected "mine\n"

cases.title: A replayed task that lists no outputs does not bring back a file the user deleted
cases.why: Nothing declared it an output; a replay that recreates it puts back bytes the user removed.

cases.title: A declared variable reaches the command
Changing a declared variable runs the task again
Going back to an earlier value restores that value’s outputs
An unset variable and an empty one are different values
`MODE` and `mode` are different variables
A variable the task does not declare changes nothing
A task with caching off runs on every run
A replayed task shows the output its run printed

choices.vx: a hit prints one line; `vx last --log <task>` shows the stored output

cases.title: Changing a task’s command runs it again
Changing a dependency’s command rebuilds the projects that read its output
Declaring a new output runs the task again so the cache holds it
cases.why: An entry saved before the output was declared does not hold it; a hit would restore a tree without it.

cases.title: Committing a change keeps the entry the uncommitted run saved
A task that exits non-zero fails the run
A failed task is not replayed as a success next time
A failed dependency stops the projects that need it from running
Fixing a failed task’s input makes the next run pass and build
A task killed by a signal fails the run and is not cached
A task that writes to stderr and exits 0 succeeds
Asking for a task no project declares fails the run
cases.why: A typo that exits 0 lets CI pass having checked nothing.

cases.title: Tasks that depend on each other in a cycle fail the run before any runs
A committed change selects its project and every project that depends on it
A change in a project nothing depends on selects only that project
With nothing changed, an affected run runs nothing and succeeds
An uncommitted edit counts as a change
A new file git does not track yet counts as a change
A deleted file counts as a change to its project
A change to a root file no task reads selects nothing
